checks: Every represented weighted point and the chosen target representative belong to the same fiber. Its diameter therefore bounds each row of the residual independently of the fiber's volume.
Summing squared row norms gives D√m and the least positive singular value applies coordinatewise on the kernel complement. The zero-matrix case has identically zero distance.

The normalized orthogonal residuals have unit Frobenius norm and lie in the affine-space orthogonal complement. Their images under T_P tend to zero, so every cluster point has the required unit norm and lies in the Jensen kernel.
When the hull has an interior site relative to its span, the Jensen and ordinary affine array spaces coincide. The same uniform estimate bounds the whole orthogonal residual.
The frozen statement matches 254a4d13e061ac3e:03 §4, (8)–(12), including arbitrary representatives in lower-dimensional nonempty fibers.

dependencies.hypotheses: The fixed lattice-complete base meets the predecessor's scope. Its vertex-row kernel and relative-interior reduction identify exactly the two spaces used in the singular-value and recession arguments. This exact predecessor needs independent approval.

overlap.comparison: The identical singular-value bound is stated for centroids of positive fibers. Arbitrary representatives of potentially null fibers and the unit cluster-point condition after quotienting by ordinary affine arrays are additional scope.

readability: The norm in the estimate is the Euclidean norm on the full vector array, equivalently the Frobenius norm.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The exact least-singular-value estimate holds for arbitrary fiber representatives and yields the claimed ordinary-affine recession subspace.
